about.title: Chino Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in Chino Hills often means a drive. With about 78,000 residents spread across the hills of southwest San Bernardino County, many people head out along Chino Hills Parkway or SR-71 to reach a hospital, surgical center, or specialist. When something goes wrong during that care, the questions start: was this a known risk, or did someone miss a step? California treats those two things very differently. Under MICRA, a poor result by itself is not malpractice. What matters is whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and whether that lapse caused real harm, and proving it nearly always requires a qualified medical expert to review the records. The clock is tight, too: generally one year from discovery, never more than three years from the injury, with a 90-day notice to the provider before any lawsuit is filed. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service connecting Chino Hills patients and families with an independent malpractice attorney who works on contingency—no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Chino Hills Patients Start With LawProactive

items.title: MICRA's Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred. Connecting early leaves room for the required 90-day pre-suit notice.

items.title: Experts Are Nearly Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert must usually confirm that care fell below the accepted standard. The attorneys we connect you with know how to obtain and evaluate that opinion before a claim moves forward.

items.title: Honest Assessment of Damages
items.desc: MICRA caps non-economic damages, though the cap rises each year, while medical bills and lost income are handled separately. An independent attorney can explain how those rules apply to your situation without overpromising.

items.question: My surgery didn't turn out the way I hoped. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not by itself. California law recognizes that medicine carries risk, so a disappointing result is only malpractice if a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that failure caused your harm. A qualified medical expert typically has to review your records to make that determination. An attorney can help you find out whether your case meets that threshold.

items.question: I was treated at a hospital outside Chino Hills. Does that matter?
items.answer: Many Chino Hills residents receive care in neighboring communities, and that is common in San Bernardino County. What matters is where and how the negligent care occurred, not where you live. An independent attorney can sort out the right venue and gather records from any facility involved.

items.question: How long do I have to act in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and never more than three years from the date of the injury itself. Before filing suit, a 90-day notice must be sent to each provider. Because those windows can overlap in confusing ways, it is wise to speak with an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.
